validation_note: Ten official or public institutional case studies. Analogies are lessons, not diagnoses for Olszówka/Gardeja.

cases.name: Lake Champlain
cases.observed_pattern: EPA identifies excess phosphorus from upland sources as a primary cause of impairment and uses phosphorus TMDLs to control loads entering the lake.
cases.management_lesson: Measure tributary loads and source contributions, not only conditions inside the lake.

provenance.title: Lake Champlain Phosphorus TMDL: A Commitment to Clean Water
provenance.supports: Excess phosphorus impairs Lake Champlain and TMDLs define load reductions for restoration.

cases.name: Upper Klamath Lake — Wood River Wetland
cases.observed_pattern: USGS reports that wetland drainage reduced marsh habitat and storage and promoted peat oxidation and nutrient release; restoration therefore requires hydrologic and water-quality management.
cases.management_lesson: A drained wetland can lose storage and become a nutrient source, so rewetting must track both water level and chemistry.

provenance.title: Hydrologic and Water-Quality Conditions During Restoration of the Wood River Wetland
provenance.supports: Drainage caused loss of marsh habitat and lake storage and altered peat biogeochemistry.

cases.name: Hoveton Great Broad
cases.observed_pattern: Natural England reports decades of nutrient enrichment and legacy pollution; restoration removed about 55,000 cubic metres of sediment before biomanipulation.
cases.management_lesson: After external pollution falls, legacy sediment and food-web effects can still require a second restoration phase.

provenance.title: Ambitious project to reverse decades of pollution in Norfolk broad
provenance.supports: Legacy pollution caused damaging algae; about 55,000 cubic metres of sediment were removed before biomanipulation.

cases.name: Danube Delta — Luncavița
cases.observed_pattern: Romania's flood planning identifies removal of a legacy dam near Luncavița to create natural retention and restore two wetlands near the Danube Delta.
cases.management_lesson: Old barriers may disconnect retention areas; any reconnection should be evaluated together with downstream flood risk.

provenance.title: Planning for resilience: Romania’s new flood risk management plans
provenance.supports: The plan recommends legacy-dam removal to create natural retention and restore two wetlands near Luncavița.

cases.name: Lake Skadar / Shkoder
cases.observed_pattern: A World Bank-supported project strengthened transboundary cooperation, ecosystem understanding, sustainable use and pollution reduction at Lake Skadar/Shkoder.
cases.management_lesson: Shared basins need common evidence and compatible rules across administrative borders.

provenance.title: Albania and Montenegro: Lake Skadar-Shkoder Integrated Ecosystem Management Project
provenance.supports: The project targets transboundary cooperation, ecosystem understanding, sustainable resource use and pollution reduction.

cases.name: Lake Toba
cases.observed_pattern: The World Bank assessment identifies deteriorating Lake Toba water quality as a core long-term environmental and economic management issue.
cases.management_lesson: Combine source inventories, field sampling and remote sensing; surface appearance alone is not proof of good water quality.

provenance.title: Lake Toba: Insights and Options for Improving Water Quality
provenance.supports: The assessment identifies water-quality deterioration as a central Lake Toba management issue.

cases.name: Lake Peipsi / Peipus
cases.observed_pattern: European Commission JRC research reports that nitrogen loading fell more than phosphorus loading while recurring cyanobacterial blooms and fish kills persisted in shallow Lake Peipsi.
cases.management_lesson: Track nitrogen, phosphorus and their ratio together; reducing one nutrient does not guarantee ecosystem recovery.

provenance.title: Reaction of Large and Shallow Lakes Peipsi and Võrtsjärv to the Changes of Nutrient Loading
provenance.supports: Persistent phosphorus and changing N/P ratios are associated with cyanobacterial blooms and fish kills in Lake Peipsi.

cases.name: Lake St Lucia Estuary
cases.observed_pattern: South Africa's expert review examined artificial breaching after prolonged mouth closure, sediment concerns and ecological change, and recommended intensive monitoring and catchment-scale management.
cases.management_lesson: Opening a connection can have system-wide effects; evaluate it with before/after monitoring and catchment context.

provenance.publisher: South Africa Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment
provenance.title: Remarks at the launch of the report reviewing the breaching of the mouth of Lake St Lucia Estuary
provenance.supports: The review addressed mouth closure, sediment, breaching and back-flooding and recommended monitoring and catchment-scale management.

cases.name: Coorong, Lower Lakes and Murray Mouth
cases.observed_pattern: Australia coordinates environmental flows through the Murray system to the Coorong, targeting healthy salinity; monitoring shows barrage flows export salt and support estuarine habitat.
cases.management_lesson: End-of-system health depends on functional through-flow and exchange, not only stored water volume.

provenance.title: Water Management Plan 2023-24: A summary
provenance.supports: Environmental flows are coordinated to the Coorong with an explicit objective of maintaining healthy salinity and ecological recovery.

cases.name: Lake Tahoe
cases.observed_pattern: EPA reports that fine sediment is the dominant driver of Lake Tahoe clarity loss, with nutrients also important; restoration quantifies source loads and includes stream and floodplain reconnection.
cases.management_lesson: Track turbidity, sediment and nutrient loads together to distinguish erosion/runoff problems from water-volume loss.

provenance.title: Lake Tahoe Water Quality Improvement Programs
provenance.supports: The Tahoe TMDL quantifies fine sediment, phosphorus and nitrogen loads and includes stream restoration and floodplain reconnection.
